terms.meaning: a Python library that checks that data has the right shape and rules before the app uses it.
a test that makes one deliberate change to valid data and checks that the program reacts correctly.
the error raised when data breaks a rule, which stops it from being used.
a connection known only from a source document, with no confirmed dates or activities.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup for network checks
sections.what: Imports the test tools and the network model, and states that these tests use no client files or outside services.
sections.why: Documents that the tests are self-contained and safe to run anywhere.

sections.name: payload
sections.title: Valid sample network
sections.what: Builds a small, consistent network with two facilities, terminals, a line between them, a coverage record and a source document reference. Every other test starts from this valid version.
sections.why: Likely reason: the other tests need one known good starting point so that each failure is caused by the single change being tested.
sections.watch_out: If this sample stops being valid, every rejection test may pass for the wrong reason.

sections.name: test_document_only_connection_has_no_invented_dates
sections.title: Connection with no invented dates
sections.what: Checks that a line known only from the document has an empty list of activities, so no dates are added that the source does not give.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app must not show schedule dates for a connection the documents do not date.
sections.watch_out: If the model fills in default activities, this test fails and the app would show dates that were never in the source.

sections.name: test_reject_false_or_unsupported_network_claim
sections.title: Each broken rule is rejected
sections.what: Runs a list of single changes to the valid network, such as a wrong coordinate, a missing terminal, a duplicate facility, an outside URL, a foreign activity, or an unknown carrier, and checks that every one raises a validation error.
sections.why: Likely reason: each change is a way the data could become false or unsafe, so each must be refused rather than shown.
sections.watch_out: Each item in the list is a separate case, so adding a new rule means adding a new case here.

summary: Checks that the programme network data model accepts only consistent, sourced, document-only connections and rejects any claim that is invented, broken, or not supported by the sources.
purpose: Keeps the network of facilities, terminals, circuits and coverage records honest, so the app never shows dates or links that the source documents do not support.
why: Likely reason: the network is built from documents, so the tests make sure invented dates or dangling references are caught before display.
how: A helper builds a valid sample network. One test confirms a document-only connection has no activities. A second test applies many single changes that each break a rule, such as a missing terminal, a foreign URL, a wrong carrier, or an activity from another project, and confirms each one is rejected.
inputs: Dictionaries built inside the test file. No client files or external services are used.
outputs: Pass or fail results. A rejected network raises a validation error.
risks: If a rule in the model is loosened, these tests will show it only for the changes listed. Any new kind of invented claim needs its own mutation entry.
debug: If a valid case is rejected, read the validation error text and compare the failing field with the payload helper. If a bad case passes, check which mutation it is and whether the model rule for that field exists.
